rubrics.justification: The model appropriately stated no image was available, but then assumed a good/excellent blastocyst (e.g., 4AA/5AA) based on patient factors rather than morphology. That is a fabricated morphological assumption not supported by the image.

It integrates most relevant factors well: young age, ovarian reserve, BMI, endometrium, unexplained infertility, sperm parameters, and first cycle status, and relates them to prognosis. It slightly overstates links between patient profile and assumed embryo quality.

The reasoning is generally structured and internally consistent, but the implantation estimate is built on an unsupported assumption of high-grade morphology and partly conflates favorable patient factors with embryo grade/euploidy likelihood.

Recommendations such as single embryo transfer in a young good-prognosis patient, luteal support, cryopreservation, and reserving PGT-A for selected scenarios are broadly guideline-consistent. Mention of ERA/immunologic testing is more controversial and not routinely recommended.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, lifestyle advice, luteal support, cryopreservation, and protocol review. Some recommendations are somewhat generic and depend on the unsupported embryo-quality assumption.
